chart_count_rule: V05a and V05b are paired panels and count as one rubric chart group.

charts.title: NSW, Victoria and Queensland hold 135 of 182 known sites

source: Geoscience Australia, Botanical Gardens and Arboretums register; snapshot 14 October 2026
transformations: Retain all 182 register features; publish point coordinates and reduced state outlines.
Classify registered hectares into four graduated size classes; retain each reported area in the tooltip.
what.measure: Registered facility footprint in hectares; not planted area, public access, collection size or conservation performance.

why.question: Where are Australia’s known botanical gardens and arboreta, and how do their registered footprints vary?
why.reader_task: Locate the known facilities and compare their register classifications and reported land areas.

how.marks: State polygons and one circle per register feature, sized with four graduated area classes.
how.channels: Projected longitude/latitude for position; discrete circle area values 12/24/48/96 for the four registered-area classes; categorical hue for Botanic Garden or Arboretum. These graduated values distinguish classes, not exact proportions; the legend gives hectare boundaries and the tooltip retains reported hectares.
how.projection: Equal Earth equal-area projection centred on Australia.
how.color: Deep blue (#003F5C) for Botanic Garden; burnt orange (#B85C00) for Arboretum.
how.ordering: Draw state outlines first, then all facility circles at 0.78 default opacity; the largest-to-smallest area ratio is 8:1. Overlap remains possible in dense locations.
how.aggregation: None; one mark per GA register feature.
how.interaction: Hover highlights the facility symbol; its tooltip identifies facility, type, locality, jurisdiction and hectares.
how.annotation: 182 known-register features: 120 Botanic Gardens and 62 Arboretums. Norfolk Island is included.

charts.title: ACT leads on known facilities per million residents

what.grain: One standard Australian state or territory; eight comparison jurisdictions.
transformations: Join GA count to ABS jurisdiction code.
Rate = facility count ÷ ERP × 1,000,000.
Keep Other Territories neutral because its one facility is on Norfolk Island and its denominator combines four non-contiguous territories.
what.measure: Known-register facilities per million residents at 31 March 2026; not access, travel distance or service quality.

why.question: How does the number of known registered facilities compare with resident population across standard jurisdictions?
why.reader_task: Compare register density without treating raw counts as equivalent across differently sized populations.

how.channels: Geographic position; sequential luminance for facilities per million residents.
how.projection: Australian conic equal-area using ASGS Edition 4 boundaries.
how.color: Light-to-dark blue for population-normalized register rates; labels use dark ink on light fills and white ink on the two darkest fills without text outlines. In linked focus, de-emphasised jurisdictions retain opaque dark labels. Neutral grey marks Other Territories with no comparative rate.
how.ordering: Continuous scale, state abbreviations and full-name tooltips.
how.aggregation: One register count and one ERP denominator per code 1–8; code 9 remains separate.
how.interaction: The linked jurisdiction selector focuses the same state on V02 and V03; hover shows count, ERP and calculated rate.
how.annotation: Rates divide facility counts by population, so smaller jurisdictions can rank higher. Other Territories combines Norfolk Island, Jervis Bay, Christmas Island and Cocos (Keeling) Islands; its grouped rate is not mapped.

charts.title: ACT rises from sixth to first after population adjustment

transformations: Rank both measures in descending order; use midrank 7.5 for the TAS/NT raw-count tie.
what.measure: Ordinal rank (1 = highest); endpoint values remain available in the tooltip.

why.question: Which jurisdictions change order when facility counts are divided by population?
why.reader_task: Follow each state between raw count rank and population-standardized rank.

how.marks: One line per jurisdiction with distinct endpoint symbols for grayscale identification.
how.channels: Horizontal position for comparison measure; vertical position for rank; color and endpoint shape redundantly identify jurisdiction.
how.color: Jurisdiction palette: NSW #005A8C, VIC #C45100, QLD #332288, WA #568EAE, SA #2D8A70, ACT #735A32, NT #444444, TAS #5D6D7E. Distinct endpoint shapes and rate-rank abbreviations repeat identity; the full-name legend supports keyboard filtering.
how.ordering: 1 is highest; the raw-count TAS/NT tie is shown at midrank 7.5. Short abbreviations sit beside the rate-rank endpoints.
how.aggregation: No aggregation beyond the two jurisdiction-level rankings.
how.interaction: Click legend items or focus a legend label and press Enter or Space to filter series; choose All jurisdictions to clear the filter. The linked jurisdiction selector highlights the same state on V02 and V03; hover reveals state, rank, raw count and rate.
how.annotation: ACT moves from rank 6 to 1, NT from midrank 7.5 to 2, and WA from 4 to 3. Rates divide counts by population; they describe register density, not access.

charts.title: A 3,739-hectare arboretum sits far outside the typical range

transformations: Group by GA subtype; compute quartiles and 1.5-IQR whiskers.
what.measure: Registered hectares on a logarithmic scale; the box spans the middle half of values.

why.question: Do Botanic Gardens and Arboretums have different registered footprint distributions?
why.reader_task: Compare typical size and spread while noticing the very large facilities.

how.marks: Horizontal box-and-whisker marks; the center line is the median, the box is the middle half, whiskers show the usual spread, and dots identify individual sites beyond them.
how.channels: Subtype on the categorical axis; logarithmic x-position for hectares; hue repeats the map’s type colors.
how.color: Green for Botanic Garden; ochre for Arboretum.
how.ordering: Botanic Garden above Arboretum; area increases left to right.
how.aggregation: Median, quartiles and 1.5-IQR whiskers computed within each type.
how.interaction: Tooltip identifies an outlier facility and its area.
how.annotation: The line marks the median; the box covers the middle half of sites. Log spacing keeps small and very large areas visible together; dots name facilities beyond the usual range.

charts.title: Seed-bank archives differ sharply in published record coverage
charts.section: 02 · Records describe different kinds of care

source: Ten ALA / Australian Virtual Seed Bank resources with CC BY 3.0 AU metadata
what.grain: Top-level accession event and distinct GBIF taxon identifier, summarized separately by resource.
transformations: Filter parentEventID blank for top-level accessions.
Count distinct taxonKey values within each resource.
Exclude dr21987, which is CC BY-NC.
what.measure: Indexed event and taxon-ID coverage by resource; neither measure is a total inventory or standardized species richness.

why.question: How much seed-bank accession and taxonomic metadata is exposed by each participating resource?
why.reader_task: Understand data coverage and why the mapped sample varies between contributors.

how.marks: Two vertically aligned horizontal dot panels, counted as one paired chart group.
how.channels: Resource on y; count on logarithmic x; separate x scales for accessions and taxon identifiers.
how.color: Muted ochre for accession rows; desaturated green-blue for taxon identifiers.
how.ordering: Resources share the same order, sorted by top-level accession count.
how.aggregation: One count and one distinct identifier count per resource; linked child events excluded.
how.interaction: Tooltip shows the full resource name, root count, distinct IDs and excluded child rows.
how.annotation: Each step on these axes is tenfold. Taxon IDs are database labels, not verified species counts; indexed records do not measure whole-bank holdings or quality.

charts.title: 1,897 PlantBank records in Myrtaceae are labelled Eucalyptus
charts.section: 02 · Records describe different kinds of care

source: GBIF PlantBank Records dataset, CC BY 4.0
what.grain: One of 10,609 occurrence rows, all marked LIVING_SPECIMEN; 10,599 have a family value.
transformations: Count original occurrence records by both family and genus.
Show five largest families with a pooled Other families parent.
Within each named family, show top four genera and an explicit Other genera remainder.
what.measure: Rectangle areas partition 10,599 indexed family-identified living-specimen records; not living plants currently held.

why.question: Which genera appear in PlantBank’s most-recorded families?
why.reader_task: Inspect genuine family-to-genus nesting and composition, not an arbitrary flat ranking.

how.marks: Parent family rectangles frame nested genus rectangles, with quantitative area, labels and thin grouping outlines.
how.channels: Nested area carries record count; a categorical family colour key distinguishes groups; names identify larger tiles.
how.color: A CVD-screened qualitative palette highlights each family group; purple consistently marks Myrtaceae (also V08), and light grey marks pooled families.
how.ordering: Families sorted by record count before deterministic binary treemap tiling; remaining families grouped as Other.
how.aggregation: Source family–genus counts reconcile exactly to 10,599 family-identified records; Other genera/families are explicit aggregates.
how.interaction: Tooltip shows family, genus/group, record count and share of family-identified records.
how.annotation: Of 3,240 PlantBank records labelled Myrtaceae, 1,897 are labelled Eucalyptus; pooled remainder tiles are groups, not taxa.

charts.title: The 1980s contain the most dated PlantBank records
charts.section: 02 · Records describe different kinds of care

source: GBIF PlantBank Records dataset, CC BY 4.0
what.grain: Individual LIVING_SPECIMEN occurrence row with a parseable year.
transformations: Parse year from year or eventDate; aggregate into decade bins.
Publish numeric decade start/end bounds (ten-year, half-open intervals).
what.measure: Records with a usable year; 9,689 rows dated 1960–2015, from 10,609 total.

why.question: Across which decades do the dated PlantBank living-specimen records fall?
why.reader_task: See the documented span and concentration of dated records without treating them as annual additions.

how.marks: Contiguous histogram bars spanning numeric ten-year intervals.
how.channels: Quantitative decade start/end bound each bin horizontally; aligned bar height shows the count.
how.color: Deep green, matching PlantBank’s living-specimen evidence.
how.ordering: Chronological decades from left to right.
how.aggregation: Count only rows with a usable four-digit year.
how.interaction: Tooltip gives exact count per decade.
how.annotation: The 1980s peak is 4,321 records; 9,689 of 10,609 PlantBank rows have usable years and 920 do not. Recorded event years are not necessarily accession dates; the series ends in 2015.

charts.title: Myrtaceae is the largest named Kings Park family
charts.section: 02 · Records describe different kinds of care

source: GBIF Kings Park Botanical Gardens dataset, CC BY 4.0
what.grain: One of 20,647 PRESERVED_SPECIMEN occurrence rows; 20,646 have a family value.
transformations: Count preserved specimen records by family; retain the 12 largest families and pool the rest.
what.measure: Indexed herbarium voucher records, not living garden holdings.

why.question: Which plant families are most frequent in the Kings Park herbarium record set?
why.reader_task: See a separate research-record layer without combining it with seed accessions or living specimens.

how.marks: Horizontal points with direct count labels.
how.channels: Count on x; family on y; Myrtaceae is highlighted.
how.color: Muted green-blue dots with the same purple Myrtaceae accent used in V06.
how.ordering: Descending specimen-record count; Other families is the final pooled row.
how.aggregation: Records grouped by family; one row equals one preserved specimen record.
how.interaction: Tooltip gives family, count and share of family-identified rows.
how.annotation: Kings Park’s 20,647 rows are PRESERVED_SPECIMEN vouchers; Myrtaceae is its largest named family. Other families pools smaller groups; these are not living holdings.

charts.title: 1,843 dated Myrtaceae records fall in the 1980s
charts.section: 02 · Records describe different kinds of care

source: GBIF PlantBank Records dataset, CC BY 4.0
what.grain: Plant family × decade among 9,683 living-specimen rows with both a usable year and family.
transformations: Count rows by family and decade; retain the ten largest families and pool the remaining families.
what.measure: Living-specimen records with both fields; dates do not measure yearly additions.

why.question: Do the main PlantBank family groups have the same recorded time span?
why.reader_task: Compare family composition across decades without mixing herbarium or seed-bank records.

how.marks: Rectangular heatmap tiles with direct positive counts.
how.channels: Family rows, chronological decade columns, sequential fill for count.
how.color: Sequential green luminance over a fixed 0–2,000-record range, with 500-record legend steps; white labels appear only on dark cells.
how.ordering: Families follow overall record count; decades follow time.
how.aggregation: Family × decade counts; 9,683 records with both fields are included.
how.interaction: Tooltip gives family, decade and record count.
how.annotation: The 1980s contain 1,843 Myrtaceae records in this dated sample; this is not a trend in conservation effort.

charts.title: 38,099 seed-origin records appear in generalized map cells

source: Ten ALA / Australian Virtual Seed Bank resources with CC BY 3.0 AU metadata
what.grain: One top-level accession event with an AU-coded usable coordinate; linked child events excluded.
transformations: Filter parentEventID blank, countryCode AU and coordinates within the Australian extent.
Project to spherical Australian Albers equal-area.
Bin to hexagons 100 km across.
Suppress cells containing fewer than five records.
what.measure: Top-level accession-origin records per public hexagon; 38,773 coordinates passed the map filter before cell suppression, 38,099 are in published cells.

why.question: Where across Australia do the licensed seed-bank resources record wild collection origins?
why.reader_task: Recognize broad source landscapes while protecting precise collection locations.

how.marks: Equal-area hexagon polygons and quiet state boundaries.
how.channels: Projected position; sequential luminance for accession-origin count per cell.
how.projection: Australian conic equal-area; bins are created in the same projection.
how.color: Teal-to-blue sequential luminance ramp over the published 5–2,629 count range; the lightest cell contrasts at least 3:1 with the neutral land background. Darker cells mean more records.
how.scale: Logarithmic transform for strongly right-skewed positive cell counts; legend ticks show 5, 20, 100, 500 and 2,629 records. Counts below five are suppressed, so no zero value is shown.
how.ordering: No ranking; map position carries geographic pattern.
how.aggregation: One 100 km-wide hex cell; records in cells below five are suppressed.
how.interaction: Tooltip gives the aggregate count; no origin point or event identifier is exposed.
how.annotation: Of 38,773 coordinate-eligible accessions, 38,099 appear in cells; 674 in cells under five are suppressed. These are recorded origins, not gardens or seed stores.

charts.title: The 2000s contain the largest dated ALA accession group

source: Ten ALA / Australian Virtual Seed Bank resources with CC BY 3.0 AU metadata
what.grain: Top-level accession event with a parseable year.
fields: parentEventID (hierarchical identifier used to exclude child events)
transformations: Filter to top-level accessions; parse a usable year; aggregate by decade.
Publish numeric decade start/end bounds (ten-year, half-open intervals).
what.measure: Dated accessions only; 33,765 of 58,562 top-level records currently have a usable year.

why.question: Across which decades do the dated seed-bank accession records fall?
why.reader_task: See the span of the dated sample without treating it as a time series of conservation activity.

how.marks: Contiguous histogram bars spanning numeric ten-year intervals.
how.channels: Quantitative decade start/end bound each bin horizontally; aligned bar height shows the count.
how.color: Muted ochre, reserved for the seed-bank evidence layer.
how.aggregation: One top-level event counted once; linked trials and other child rows excluded.
how.interaction: Tooltip gives the decade and exact count.
how.annotation: 33,765 of 58,562 top-level accessions have usable event years across six resources; four have none. The 2020s end in 2025; dates are not annual collecting effort.

charts.title: Map-ready coordinates range from zero to full coverage

transformations: Map-ready share = valid AU-coded coordinate pairs inside the national extent ÷ top-level accessions.
what.measure: Percentage of top-level accession records ready for the origin map.

why.question: Is the origin map based on the same share of records for each contributor?
why.reader_task: Judge how uneven coordinate availability may shape the visible pattern.

how.marks: Horizontal bars with endpoint dots and printed percentages.
how.channels: Resource on y; percentage with map-ready coordinates on x.
how.color: Muted olive; this is data completeness, not conservation quality.
how.aggregation: One numerator and root-accession denominator per resource.
how.interaction: Tooltip gives map-ready count, total roots and percentage.
how.annotation: Map-ready coordinates range from 0% in Alice Springs to 100% in Darwin; in the ALA Australian PlantBank archive, 2,921 of 12,871 top-level accessions (22.7%) lack them. Completeness is metadata availability, not geographic representativeness.

charts.title: Four of ten archives lack usable collection years

what.grain: One resource summarized across top-level accessions with a usable year.
transformations: Filter parentEventID blank; parse dates; compute minimum and maximum year per resource.
what.measure: Documented year coverage within each archive; resources without parseable years are listed separately.

why.question: Do participating seed-bank resources cover the same recorded time span?
why.reader_task: Understand the limits of the combined dated-record histogram.

how.marks: Horizontal range rules with endpoint circles.
how.channels: Year on x; resource on y; rule length encodes min-to-max year span.
how.color: Muted ochre, consistent with seed-bank records.
how.ordering: Resources sorted by earliest year; one-year spans remain visible as points.
how.aggregation: Minimum and maximum parseable year per resource.
how.interaction: Tooltip gives date bounds, dated count and root-accession total.
how.annotation: Four archives lack usable top-level years; ranges are observed file endpoints, not continuous collecting activity.
